long_biography.plain_text:
A teenage apprenticeship at a Hatton Garden workbench gave Laurence Graff his entry into jewellery manufacture. When a later employer failed, he started a small partnership repairing Victorian pieces, then used credit to buy diamonds and developed his own designs. He established Graff in 1960 and opened its first two London boutiques two years later, turning workshop skills and direct selling into an international retail business.

Graff subsequently brought more of the diamond chain inside the group, combining rough-diamond procurement, cutting and polishing, jewellery manufacture and boutique retail. That integrated model, together with continuing private control, is the foundation of his fortune. Laurence Graff remains the company's founder and chairman and continues to exercise significant control over the business. Francois Graff serves as chief executive, distinguishing the founder's ownership and strategic position from current operating management.
